items.title: Andhra CM announces Rs 10 lakh compensation for families of 8 killed in Palnadu crash
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu has announced an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh each for the families of the eight people who died in a road accident at Chilakaluripet in Palnadu district. He directed officials to provide the assistance to the bereaved families at the earliest. The accident took place in the early hours of August 27 at Addaroad Centre in Chilakaluripet town after a private bus collided with an auto-rickshaw carrying 15 people in Palnadu district. The victims, all residents of Veluru village in Chilakaluripet mandal, were travelling in an auto-rickshaw after attending a birthday celebration. According to the police, the group was returning to Veluru after travelling to Konda Manjuluru village in J Panguluru mandal of Prakasam district. There were 15 people in the auto, including four children, nine women and two men. As the auto-rickshaw was taking a turn at Addaroad Centre, a private travel bus travelling from Vijayawada towards Tirupati collided with it. The impact left several passengers seriously injured. items.title: Karnataka extends Gruha Jyothi verification deadline by a month to Sept 30
items.summary: The Karnataka government has extended the deadline for the door-to-door verification of Gruha Jyothi scheme beneficiaries by a month, with the survey now set to continue until September 30. The review survey began on July 1, with August 31 being the original deadline. As of May 2026, there were 68.86 lakh Gruha Jyothi beneficiaries across the eight districts under the Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Ltd. (BESCOM). Of these, 46.7 lakh, or about 70%, had been surveyed by August 31. BESCOM Managing Director N Shivashankara has urged the remaining beneficiaries to cooperate with meter readers and provide the required documents when officials visit their homes from September 1. According to BESCOM officials, some beneficiaries living in apartments in Bengaluru had not been cooperating with survey staff. Apartment residents have been asked to facilitate access for officials visiting their premises. For locked houses, meter readers will make up to three visits at different times.
